recipes.name: Campbell’s Tuna Noodle Casserole
ingredients_raw: 4 cups hot cooked medium egg noodles
2 (10.5 ounce) cans Campbell's® Condensed Cream of Mushroom Soup (regular or 25% Lower Sodium)

steps.text: Gather all ingredients and preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Stir cooked noodles, condensed soup, tuna, peas, and milk in a 3-quart casserole.
Bake in the preheated oven until hot, about 30 minutes; stir well.
Mix bread crumbs with melted butter in a bowl; sprinkle over tuna casserole and continue to bake until bread crumbs are golden brown and crispy, 5 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Campbell’s Tuna Noodle Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This tuna noodle casserole uses mushroom soup to add flavor to a creamy sauce that’s mixed with noodles, tuna, and peas to make this family favorite.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make Campbell's Tuna Noodle Casserole—a classic comfort food that's easy to make and sure to please. This recipe uses creamy condensed cream of mushroom soup to make a savory sauce that's mixed with tender egg noodles, meaty tuna, and sweet peas. Topped with a crunchy bread crumb crust, this casserole is baked to perfection and sure to become a family favorite. With simple ingredients and easy-to-follow directions, it's no wonder why this recipe earned a stellar rating!

review.reviewBody: Why, oh why do people skimp on the crumb topping and spices? Make it better with this: 1/2 c crackers, 1/4 wedge of parmesean cheese, and 2 tbls cold butter. Puree it all in a food processor and add it at the beginning of the cooking time - then it's crispy and great, and also keeps those top noodles from getting icky and crunchy if they stick out the top of the casserole. A little garlic powder, thyme, and shallots can't hurt this recipe, either!

i love this meal. But I did make changes. I used french fried onion rings broken up into small pieces. I mixed this with the noodles, milk. Peas and tuna. At the end I added cheese and more french fried onion rings. Quick and easy for a comfort meal on a cold day in Ohio.

Just like I remember from a kid.....substituting shredded cheese and crushed potato chips for the butter and bread crumb ingredients. Sprinkle a little fresh parmesan on the individual servings....delicious
Made it easily, added corn, 🍄, cheese soup, grated 3 cheese, spinich. Turned out awesome 👍.
Pretty bland so you have to add some seasonings. NOT potato chips, bacon, sausage and all the other garbage people are adding to make it a Fat Tuesday meal. Jeeeeez.

This recipe is good but with a few extras its amazing!!! I followed the directions but I used one can tuna one can chicken then I read some reviews and added some seasonings: garlic powder, Italian seasoning and some pepper (an even layer of each over the casserole) and I added 1 finely chopped shallot (from another review) and french's fried onion, I mixed them inside and I put the rest on top. I used canned carrots, peas, and frozen corn (because that's what I had in the cabinet). I used shelled pasta instead of egg noodle as well. And I topped it with Cheddar and parmesan the last five min. IT WAS AMAZING!!! AND MY PICKY 4 YR. OLD LOVED IT! thank you for the reviews everyone they helped alot! This recipe is a keeper!!!

A tasty childhood comfort food! I followed the advice of other home cooks and amped up the flavor by adding one medium onion chopped and sautéed (the sautéing is important to do before adding other ingredients), red pepper flakes, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper to the tuna mix. I reduced the peas to one cup as two seemed a bit much and replaced the American cheese slices with one and a half cups of grated red and white sharp cheddar and finished in the oven for 15. Super simple, yummy - perfect for a lazy Sunday dinner with plenty of leftovers for the week!
I always sautee chopped onions, celery & fresh mushrooms, & add these plus 1 cup of sharp shredded cheddar cheese. I increase baking time as needed, until hot & bubbly then add the bread topping.

I added sliced mushrooms, onions & celery, (I pan- fried all fresh produce before adding to the casserole, while my noodles were boiling). I pre-cooked my egg noodles with 2 cubes of chicken bouillon then used crushed Lays potato chips gently tossed with some grated cheddar cheese and parsley for the topping. Definitely not a low-cal meal, but everyone in the house loved it!

Good base recipe. Bland unless you spice it up. I added 1 tbsp garlic and onion powder and black pepper to the casserole. Mixed in fresh shiitake mushrooms & 2 stalks chopped celery and 1/2 cup shredded Sargento Mexican blended cheese with the frozen peas. Used 1 cup Panko bread crumbs mixed with entire cube of melted butter for a thick layer over the top -back in oven for 7 minutes at the end. I'm trying to cut salt down or I'd use the potato chips. The crunchy breadcrumbs made a delicious difference. So yummy I ate 2 big bowls myself. Next time I'll sauté an onion and the mushroom in EVO first and add a little cayenne to the spices. The tuna adds protein but to be honest I couldn't really taste it. You could put canned chicken in and probably wouldn't know the difference. You could make this with penne, orzo, white rice but the extra wide noodles are the best. It's a good base recipe with many possible variations.

Made this yesterday, and it was okay. A bit dry, but that could have been that I did half recipe in a medium casserole dish. Next time I'll use a smaller dish, and add more milk. I didn't use pimentos, but I did use the extra small peas. I added cheddar cheese to the mixture too like most others, and black pepper. Today, I did a half recipe but instead of regular tuna, I put in a can of Spicy Thai flavoured tuna, and it was YUMMMM! For a full recipe, I'd use one regular can of tuna, and one of the Spicy Thai.

I grew up with having this for dinner in the 1950's and 1960's, so it was one of the first recipes I cooked when I moved into my apartment. I make it according to the basic recipe and because it is so customizable I have this with many different versions. I use low-salt or heart healthy soups to make it and no added salt.

I followed the recipe but doubled up on the bread crumbs plus butter. Also, I used store bought crumbs that have Italian seasoning. I made the entire bag of egg noodles and it turned out to be a good amount to fill the rectangular pyrex cake pan that I used.
I used a can of sardines to ram up the fish flavor with the tuna! YUM

this is so basic, I've made it since 1966 and also add Kraft cracker barrel extra sharp cheddar cheese, the whole bar of it. Like 8 ounces...love the cheese with it....so much less boring. ( cube cut up the cheese)
delicious, easy, satisfying
I made it exactly as written except I seasoned the mixture before adding to baking dish and I added cheddar cheese instead of bread crumb mixture. Very good comfort food. Thank you.

Good recipe although 2 tablespoons of breadcrumbs and 1 tablespoon of melted butter hardly seem enough for a 3-quart casserole. I add chopped onions, which sometimes I sauté first; tonight, I chopped up some carrot and sautéed it along with the onions. I’ve been making this recipe for years.
This is a wonderful recipe. I sometimes add French fried onions on the top until golden brown instead of breadcrumbs.

This recipe was very easy to follow and has lots of great flavor. My family loves it! The only thing I did differently was add about 1/4 cup of shredded carrot and topped it with shredded Parmigiano-Reggiano. Delicious!
